title: Quality Attributes and Code Reviews
learningObjectives: Explain the concept and its role in reliable software.
Identify the topic in code or a realistic scenario.
Trace behavior and describe the expected result.
Apply the concept and verify it using a suitable test.

understand.concept: Software quality includes correctness, reliability, maintainability, usability, accessibility, performance, security, compatibility, and testability. A code review examines a change for these qualities, its logic, risks, clarity, and consistency with requirements. Reviews complement automated checks and testing; they do not replace them.
understand.whyItMatters: A solution can produce correct output for one case while being hard to maintain, inaccessible, unsafe, slow, or fragile. Reviewing broader quality attributes improves the overall product.
understand.analogy: A careful process uses defined expectations, evidence, and repeatable checks to reduce uncertainty.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy simplifies software quality; the actual techniques depend on project context, tools, architecture, and risk.

explain.narrative: Review the requirement and scope, inspect the diff, check correctness and edge cases, assess security and accessibility implications, look for maintainability and test gaps, and provide specific respectful feedback. Prefer actionable findings tied to evidence; separate blockers from suggestions.

examples.title: Risk-based review
examples.explanation: Sensitive areas deserve focused review of assumptions and failure paths.

examples.code:

console.log(feedback);

examples.explanation: Specific review feedback points to an observable improvement.

commonMistakes: Vague comments without an actionable point.
Treating personal style preference as a defect.
Ignoring accessibility, security, or performance context.
Assuming code review replaces automated tests.
